intro: The honeypot caught something at 03:14, and the red team knew at once it was not an attacker. It was a message, split across every protocol the intruder could find, carried on noise that made the LEDs shiver and the air taste of static. A half-finished cup of tea sat beside a keyboard sprayed with fingerprints, and the newest analyst kept rubbing sleep from her eyes. On the shelf above the bench sits a compositor's case, and the red team treats found artefacts the way an old printer treats its case: every piece has its place. They leave the pieces there overnight, trusting the room to keep its own counsel until morning.
echo: Software with bad intentions, which is all its name means.

puzzles.title: Null Byte
puzzles.flavor: Rubbings from a handrail. Unlucky for some, and the same distance either way.

partials.784c623814d2dfb3bb6a65360a3f01dce118e10d: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Write each number in binary. Six yes-or-no choices: is there an alphabet built from exactly that? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: Rubber Ducky
puzzles.flavor: Each column remembers what it held, but not in what order.
hints: Black squares are spaces. Which two- and three-letter words fit, using only the letters each column allows?

puzzles.title: Privilege Escalation
puzzles.flavor: Bunting on the halyard, and not for a celebration.
hints: Ships carry a flag for every letter of the alphabet. Do you know them?

puzzles.title: Air Gap
puzzles.flavor: It never travels in a straight line, and neither does the truth. Something in here has been through the looking glass.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from h3: Ng5 Nh7 Nf8 Nd7 Nc5 Nb3 Nd4.

partials.299122c75a44a155a5dfee31e8e43431e83f4a54: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: Salted Hash
puzzles.flavor: Everything in its place, and nothing twice.
hints: A familiar grid puzzle in unfamiliar clothes. Once it's done, are some squares more important than others?

puzzles.title: Man In The Middle
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?

puzzles.title: Rainbow Table
puzzles.flavor: The machine keeps its diary in your cells' alphabet, if your cells could only say yes or no.
hints: How many different things can a pair of bits say? Four is a very biological number.

meta.title: Meta: Capture The Flag
meta.flavor: Pigeonholes, each cut to fit one thing only.
hints: The grid's rows are all different lengths. So are your answers.
